speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Singapore has developed rapidly over the last 55 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: And we need to ensure that our building infrastructure remains well-maintained and safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition, our buildings, both old and new, will need to be made more accessible to meet the needs of an ageing population, as well as persons with disabilities (PWDs).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It is in this context that we are proposing amendments to the Building Control Act, to strengthen the building control regulatory framework and to improve accessibility of our built environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the Building Control Act sets out the duties of relevant parties, such as owners, developers, builders and professionals at the design and construction stages of a building.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, at the design stage, the developer is required to submit building and structural plans to BCA for approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At the construction stage, a Qualified Person is required to supervise the works to ensure that buildings are constructed according to the approved plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: But after a building is completed, there are also requirements to maintain the building so that it is safe to use.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These requirements pertaining to maintenance are currently in the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act (BMSMA).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It gives the Commissioner of Buildings the power to compel owners to carry out repairs to a building that is not properly maintained.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It also gives the Minister the powers to enact regulations pertaining to the operation and maintenance of lifts and escalators (L&E).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The BMSMA will be renamed the Building (Strata Management) Act to better reflect its revised scope.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This consolidation will facilitate BCA's oversight over the various building-related processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It will also allow us to strengthen the building control regulatory framework to improve safety and accessibility in a holistic manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Besides this consolidation, the Bill contains amendments to the Building Control Act which broadly covers the following three areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, it will provide for a building facade inspection regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: And last, but not least, it will accelerate accessibility upgrading in existing buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We need to ensure that they are designed, installed and maintained properly, so that they are safe to use.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is important as we rely on them in our everyday lives, to get home, to get to work, or simply to get to town.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the regulatory regime focuses on L&E maintenance and operation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, for example, BCA mandates their maintenance frequency and outcomes, requires annual inspection and testing of the L&E, as well as for owners to apply for a permit to operate annually.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Upstream, BCA requires professional engineers to certify that the design and installation of L&E are done according to industry codes and standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We propose to strengthen BCA's upstream regulatory oversight for L&E, to reduce the likelihood of deficiencies in design or installation which may give rise to downstream safety incidents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Broadly, we will do this by extending the existing design and construction regime for buildings to L&E installations as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This approach is consistent, given that L&E are integral parts of our buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, clauses 2 and 3 will empower BCA to require L&E professionals to submit design plans for L&E works to BCA for approval just as they would for building works.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: L&E professionals will then need to ensure that the L&E are installed according to the approved plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Penalties for L&E offences will be aligned with those for existing building offences of a similar nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, the Minister will have powers to enact regulations to prescribe the key requirements of L&E design and installation, as well as the corresponding duties of stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, we intend to require L&E professionals to ensure that the lift model and its key safety components are certified by independent certification bodies, as part of the new plan submission process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At the same time, we will also enhance BCA's ability to improve safety for both new and existing L&E installations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, under clause 21, relevant parties, such as L&E owners and contractors, will be required to notify BCA of any safety-related defects they may become aware of.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For instance, contractors may come across manufacturing defects during the maintenance of a particular lift.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: They will need to inform BCA so that BCA can get the L&E owners to rectify the defects in this lift and to check other similar lifts to make sure that such defects are not systemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 20 will allow the Commissioner of Building Control to issue orders to L&E owners to prevent safety incidents from occurring.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For instance, when a check has revealed that there is an imminent safety risk arising from poor design or installation, the Commissioner of Building Control can issue an order to the owner to stop operating the lift or escalator until the risk has been mitigated or removed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will supplement existing powers to require L&E owners to address maintenance-related issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, clause 16 will allow the Minister to mandate the retrofitting of existing L&Es, for example, if certain models of L&E or their components are prone to incidents that affect public safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Bill also increases the range of levers available against errant L&E contractors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, the Commissioner of Building Control can censure or suspend the contractor, revoke the contractor's registration, impose composition sums or prosecute them.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For instance, suspending or revoking the registration of a contractor may have unintended safety implications if L&E owners are not able to find an alternative contractor to maintain their L&E.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: On the other hand, simply censuring or imposing financial penalties may not be sufficient to resolve the underlying concerns for public safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: An errant contractor could continue to also take on more L&E jobs without carrying out internal improvements to meet the required standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Thus, clause 36 introduces a registration scheme for L&E contractors and sets out additional regulatory sanctions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Basically, it goes beyond just the machinery but also the standard of employees that may need to maintain our L&Es.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 36 also introduces a new section 29Q, which is needed for the L&E industry to be able to attract and retain competent technicians and engineers to ensure that our L&Es are safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The L&E industry faces the challenges today of an ageing workforce and they also have difficulty in attracting new entrants, especially younger technicians.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In January 2017, an L&E Sectoral Tripartite Committee (STC) was formed to look into the sector's manpower challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This committee, co-chaired by NTUC and BCA, comprised representatives from Government agencies, industry associations and unions, as well as service buyers and providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: One of its key recommendations was to introduce a progressive wage model (PWM) for the lift industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The PWM seeks to increase basic wages across the board for local lift technicians, particularly at the lower levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The recommended wages are pegged against comparable technician jobs in other sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The PWM also creates clear career progression paths and ensures that wages are commensurate with the job responsibilities and competencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Government accepted the STC's recommendation in September 2018 and announced that we would work towards mandating PWM adoption for lift maintenance firms.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: From May 2019, Government Procuring Entities have taken the lead by only awarding lift maintenance tenders to firms that have adopted the PWM.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: BCA has been working with industry stakeholders to implement the PWM and the associated training and certification framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We encourage the remaining firms to adopt the PWM early as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Going beyond the lift industry, MOM has recently announced the Tripartite Cluster for Lift and Escalator Industry, which will look into a PWM for escalator maintenance technicians.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We expect the Tripartite Cluster to provide its recommendations by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Besides reviewing the regulatory framework for lifts for people, we also reviewed the regulatory framework for Mechanised Car Parking Systems (MCPS).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These are automated car lifting systems that transport a car, without its driver, to and from a parking area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: BCA does not regulate the operation and maintenance of MCPS today.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, BCA has found that these systems could potentially pose a danger to users.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, some MCPS do not have measures to prevent unauthorised access into the transfer areas, which pose a safety concern should users get trapped in the parking area.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Thus, clause 45 amends section 49 to enable the Minister to enact regulations for MCPS to enhance user safety.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Our current intent is to regulate only areas where users directly interface with the equipment, such as the car transfer area, and the operating panel for parking and retrieval.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, owners and persons responsible have a duty to ensure that building exteriors are kept in good and serviceable repair and that exterior features are securely fixed.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In this regard, general maintenance works are already carried out regularly on building facades.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These works can include simple rectifications, general cleaning as well as painting of external walls.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, there is a need for us to further improve the facade maintenance standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Most of these were related to the wear and tear of the facade materials or connections.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Thus, we will put in place a more structured approach towards the inspection and maintenance of building facades.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will help guide owners in meeting their existing duty regarding facade maintenance.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clauses 23, 24 and 25 amend the present Part V of the Building Control Act to introduce a new Periodic Facade Inspection regime that will require owners to engage professionals to check their building facades regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will help to detect signs of facade deterioration early and facilitate timely repairs to reduce the likelihood of facade failure.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This takes into consideration the expected lifespan of some facade materials.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It is also aligned with the typical length of Repair and Redecoration cycles for HDB estates and condominium developments, to save costs and reduce inconvenience to residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: BCA will introduce inspection guidelines and strengthen R&D efforts to look into more effective and productive ways to carry out facade inspections.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition to the new facade inspection regime, the Bill will also introduce requirements for the relevant parties to report safety-related defects as well as incidents relating to facades.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is similar to our approach with the L&Es.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We first introduced accessibility requirements for new buildings in 1990, with a Code on Barrier-free Accessibility in Buildings.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In consultation with representatives from social service agencies, trade associations and chambers as well as Government agencies, the Code has undergone several revisions over the years to ensure that the provisions address the evolving needs of Singaporeans, taking reference from international standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Besides new buildings, the Code also applies to existing buildings that undergo addition and alteration (A&A) works.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, the current requirements only apply at the specific locations in the building where the A&A works are undertaken.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, if A&A works are carried out to renovate the washrooms on the upper floor of a building, we can require that the washrooms of that floor be made accessible.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As can be seen from the sheet, Tong Building, IOB Building and Bukit Merah Community Centre are among some examples of buildings that provide basic accessibility features on their own accord.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These features refer to an accessible building entrance, an accessible route at the entrance level and at least one toilet in the building with lift access if the accessible toilet is on another floor.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We should do more to ensure that our existing buildings are made accessible to all, whenever A&A works are undertaken.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, almost all of our public sector buildings and infrastructure that are frequented by the general public have achieved at least basic accessibility.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Examples include offices, hotels, schools and shopping centres.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will exclude smaller buildings, such as shop houses, from these requirements because there is space constraints.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Bill will also make other changes to improve and clarify the Builder licensing scheme and to facilitate BCA's operations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Licensed builders need to have an "approved person" who is responsible for the management of the business.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These amendments will also allow more types of businesses to apply for a Builder's licence, including sole proprietors and partnerships comprising corporations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will provide greater flexibility for the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, smaller firms will be able to form partnerships to take on projects beyond their individual capacity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope Er Dr Lee Bee Wah is happy that more local firms can participate in bigger projects, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This includes restricting the builder from taking on any new project or any new project above a certain value.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The rationale for this change is similar to what I had earlier described – to enhance the measures to regulate L&E contractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: A few clauses will improve the clarity of the legislation to facilitate the administration of the Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Clause 8 amends section 11 to make it it clear that builders need to notify the Commissioner of Building Control of the appointment or termination of a specialist builder within 14 days and that builders are accountable for the works that they subcontract out.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Clause 27 amends section 29A to make clear that builders need not be licensed if they are always carrying on their business as sub-contractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Clause 20 will require owners in non-strata titled buildings to jointly appoint a Qualified Person (QP) for the purpose of complying with BCA's orders, if such orders are served on multiple owners.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will avoid a situation where each owner engages its own QP, which may result in different recommendations and delays in complying with BCA's orders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA has consulted industry stakeholders, including building owners, contractors and professionals, on the key changes through more than 10 engagement sessions over the last four years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The industry stakeholders were supportive of the changes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will continue to work closely with the industry to implement the changes proposed in this Bill, which will enhance safety and accessibility in our built environment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I support the amendments for proper registration and training of lift technicians.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We know individual lift companies may have their own in-house training, but how adequate are these training sessions?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is also a lack of career path for the technicians.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, you do not attract jobseekers and there would be job-hopping, maybe leading to staff who are not adequately trained.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next, how do we regulate that the technical crew are not pressured to do jobs in a hurried manner or jobs they are not trained to do, because they have to meet a quota of servicing X number of lifts in a day?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Based on my observation in Nee Soon South, definitely, there is a lot of room for improvement in the quality of lift maintenance and quality of service by lift companies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Sometimes, they even shut down the lift without putting up proper signage and proper notice to the residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Sometimes, soon after the lift is back to order, back to working condition, then it breaks down again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It just shows that the checking was not thorough enough and that caused a lot of inconvenience to the residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Also, I believe there is a great shortage of technicians and engineers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is why they hurriedly finish the work and then put it back into service again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is the target number and the schedule of rolling out?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How many qualified trainers do we have to conduct courses on lift maintenance?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are we also training more lift engineers, too?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These are very specialised systems and they need to be properly installed and maintained.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Again, how many competent people are there to conduct the training?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And how long does it take to get someone trained?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think one important consideration is the frequency of the usage, rather than just a standard timeframe maintenance schedule.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many building owners may want fanciful facades to make their structures stand out.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But this is where aesthetics may be achieved at the expense of practicality of maintenance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have our share of awnings and claddings on façades falling off.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is the protocol for the maintenance of these structures?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How are the workers trained for such roles?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   In 2018, there were several lift breakdown incidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, I support the Government to strengthen the regulation of this industry.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: From what I have observed, lift maintenance is hard work and there are few career progress opportunities.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This could have resulted in the situation whereby people are not interested in positions in this industry.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is going to affect the quality of maintenance, and subsequently public safety.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, we do not know what the quality of training is like in the various companies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, to establish a training and registration system for the technicians can ensure public safety better.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Every now and then, we have episodes of claddings and awnings on facades falling off.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As an urban and densely built-up society, public safety of building structures and fixed installations are critical.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That said, these measures will entail costs, which will be a concern to those responsible, including Town Councils.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Member Mr Fasal Manap, who chairs the Aljunied-Hougang Town Council, will elaborate further in his speech.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wish to seek clarifications on two particular aspects of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first clarification is on the maintenance of exterior features of buildings.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This Bill simplifies the definition of “exterior feature” to mean any permanent feature of a building that is installed on, forms part of or projects outwards from the roof or exterior of the building, and such other features that may be prescribed in the regulations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This is an improvement from the existing definition which contains a laundry list of features.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I note that the Bill changes the definition of the person responsible to maintain these features.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Under the existing Act, it is stated that for HDB blocks, the person responsible to maintain exterior features is either the HDB or the Town Council, depending on who the Minister designates for that feature.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, what is the rationale of removing HDB from the definition as a person responsible for the exterior feature?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does this amendment change the responsibility of HDB towards problematic features?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: An exterior feature could have been unsafe from the point of construction; alternatively, it could become unsafe over time due to wear and tear or lack of maintenance, in which case, Town Councils will have to bear some responsibility.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What is the implication of removing HDB from the definition of “person responsible” for maintaining an exterior feature?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question relates to the inclusion of the Town Council’s contractor as a “person responsible”, if that contractor has charge and control of the management and maintenance of the common property.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does this phrase mean a Town Council’s Managing Agent, where a Town Council has outsourced its operations to an MA?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The same section makes it clear that for private property, such as condominiums, managing agents are persons responsible together with the owners.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could Ministry explain why, for HDB estates, the phrase “managing agent” is not used?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These duties include the need to comply with BCA’s Notices to Maintain under the new section 25E, at their cost.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They also have duties to report safety incidents under the new section 25B, and failure to perform these duties carries heavy responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Clause 20 provides for situations where the Commissioner of Building Control requires an owner to inspect and take remedial actions in respect of a potentially dangerous building, exterior feature or fixed installation, or a building product that carries a safety risk.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This will expand the class of persons who do such work beyond architects and professional engineers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What is the thinking behind apparently relaxing this requirement as we are dealing here with potentially dangerous structures and safety concerns?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will the Ministry provide guidance as to the alternative qualifications that such an appropriate person should have?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Professionals from the lift industry have shared with me that lift maintenance is known as a "3D" industry – it is dark, dirty and dangerous.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three clarifications on the Bill relating to: (a) facilities for persons with disabilities (PWDs); (b) the progressive wage model (PWM) framework; and (c) working conditions for lift technicians.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, buildings that are used solely for residential purposes or as a factory are excluded from this section 22DA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share the rationale for excluding residential and factory buildings which are premises that PWDs will need to access?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If residential and factory buildings are excluded from section 22DA, can the Minister share how it intends to ensure that building owners of residential and factory buildings will install features for access by PWDs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, the Commissioner can only require building owners to include features for PWDs if it receives an application from the building owner for approval of plans for the alternation, addition or repair of a relevant building.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will mean that the progress of ensuring that our buildings are PWD-friendly is dependent on the building owners deciding to undertake building works.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share whether it has a target for ensuring that most, if not all, buildings in Singapore are PWD-friendly?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What plans does the Ministry have to encourage building owners to include PWD-friendly facilities?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The reality is that lift companies have a large number of foreigners because of a severe shortage of lift technicians, given the difficult working conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lift technicians who are foreigners are doing jobs that are equally as difficult and equally as dangerous as the jobs Singaporeans and PRs are doing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is not just an issue of fairness, but one of safety and incentives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do we want lift technicians who have to ensure the safety of lifts that we all take multiple times a day to feel disgruntled and that their colleague doing the exact same job is paid much higher than he or she is?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In October 2018, during the debate on the Environmental Public Health (Amendment) Bill, I spoke about the need to ensure that the PWM will apply to cleaners who are hired directly by an F&B establishment and for foreign cleaners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I highlighted that PWM is about increasing productivity and standards and if we leave out our foreign cleaners from the PWM, bear in mind again that foreign cleaners likely form a bulk of the cleaning sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This similarly applies to the lift technicians industry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MEWR has encouraged employers to incorporate the principles of progressive wages into the wage structure of their foreign cleaners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will MND take similar steps to encourage the incorporation of PWM principles into the contracts for foreign lift technicians?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Or will the Ministry also consider eventually extending the PWM to cover foreign lift technicians?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just in January this year, Minister Chan Chun Sing said “The real competition is Team Singapore, comprising Singaporeans, PRs and foreign workers here, competing with the rest of the world to give our fellow Singaporeans the best chance possible to win, not just in Singapore but across the entire globe." How can we say that we are Team Singapore if we discriminate against certain team members?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will a team work together well if we do not reward the same effort and merit with the same pay?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Ministry has accepted the recommendations in late 2018.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that BCA is also studying the feasibility of improving ventilation within the lift shaft and motor room to create a cooler work environment for the maintenance personnel.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share its progress in implementing these recommendations to improve working conditions for lift technicians?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister also share details on how it intends to implement these other recommendations?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I welcome these amendments as safety is paramount and should not be taken lightly.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In recent years, we have heard and seen news on a number of cases that pertains to dislodgement of fixtures from HDB blocks' facade or exterior wall such as sunshades, decoratives and even bricks.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, this is not the case for lift malfunction-related incidents that occurred in HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In the last few years, there has been reports of residents or members of the public who are visiting, sustaining mild to serious injuries.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I do hope with the tightening of legislation and measures as proposed in this Amendment Bill, it will provide a safer and more conducive living environment.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Nonetheless, as the Chair of Aljunied-Hougang Town Council, I do have concerns on the cost issue.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Consequently, the adoption and the implementation of the new measures and regimes indicated in this Bill will be the additional expenditure.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We have encountered dislodgement of facade, fixtures, and one of these incidents was cited by my colleague Mr Pritam Singh two days ago during MND's Committee of Supply's debate.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Another point I want to raise is on availability of trained personnel or an appropriate person as mentioned in clause 20 on building inspections and other building works.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This issue was touched on earlier by my colleague Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I would just like to seek the Ministtry's views on whether there will be any possibility of shortage of this appropriate person due to the enhanced measurements and regime introduced in this Bill, as there will be a higher demand for such individuals?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In short, will there be an issue of imbalanced supply and demand situation, in particular, for the mandatory regime of facade inspection?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If this shortage is likely to happen, what will be the Ministry's plan to address this issue?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am currently the Chairman of the Tripartite Cluster for Lift & Escalator Industry but I would like to state that the expressed views in my speech are my own and not a representation of the committee’s view.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This workforce maintains more than 70,000 lifts and 7,000 escalators every day.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Maintenance personnel make up most of the sector’s workforce and are essential in providing day-to-day servicing to ensure lifts are well-maintained for safe and reliable use.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In 2017, the Lift and Escalator Sectoral Tripartite Committee chaired by my fellow Labour Member of Parliament, Mr Melvin Yong, was formed comprising representatives from the Government, trade unions, industry associations and firms, and service buyers.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Committee has now been tasked to review the escalator industry and renamed the Tripartite Cluster for Lift and Escalator, which I am chairing, together with a co-chair from Singapore National Employers’ Federation, Mr Tony Khoo, CEO of EM Services.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: One of the recommendations put up by the first Tripartite Committee was the Progressive Wage Model to uplift the wages of the workers in the lift industry that commensurate with their skills, productivity and career progression.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Based on my experience implementing PWM in the other sectors, engagement with Service Providers and Service Buyers are critical before the start of the full implementation to ensure the stakeholders will factor in possible cost implications in the contract pricing.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Of these 95, the top 12 firms or close to 13% of them command 86% of the market share.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Similarly, for the escalator industry, there are 31 firms, with the top 11 firms maintaining 95% of the escalators in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This industry seems to have an oligopoly market structure with a few firms dominating the market.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This state of oligopoly arises because the major players can exert proprietary rights over their spare parts and are not required to disclose the technical specifications of the lift systems.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, many of the lift technicians can only service lifts made by their companies.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Such practices hinder market competition to the disadvantage of lift owners and discourage job mobility amongst the lift technicians as they do not have the knowledge and skills to service different types of lifts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Building owners often are compelled to award their maintenance contracts to the OEM lift firms for fear that other non-OEM companies would not be able to secure spare parts or have the experienced technicians to do troubleshooting and repair.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the European Union countries, the lift industry is encouraged to adopt an open and non-proprietary lift system which will serve to level the playing field and promote greater market competition.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would also allow the lift and escalator technicians to be cross-trained in different types of lifts and escalators.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Moving forward, I would like to know whether BCA will consider open and non-proprietary system in our lift and escalator industry and make the necessary legislative amendments to make this possible.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Lift and Escalator industry, as shared by my fellow Member of Parliament is often perceived as having the 4 Ds – Difficult, Dirty, Dark and Dangerous.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, the Lift and Escalator Sectoral Tripartite Committee also formed a working committee and one of the committee’s terms of reference was to propose and develop solutions to improve key aspects of working conditions to enhance attractiveness of the job to new entrants.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The working committee made several recommendations to improve the thermal comfort, illuminance level, and safety and ease of maintenance at working places on the lift.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Based on the new amendment to this Bill under clause 20, section 24, will it give the authority to Commissioner of Building Control to compel lift owners to retrofit their existing lifts?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the cost of retrofitting new lifts to improve the work environment for the lift technicians can be very expensive, will there be funding support for such work to be carried out?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The cost of retrofitting on existing buildings can be substantial, especially for Town Council managing HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, it would certainly help if all new HDB estates could take this into consideration at the planning and design stage, and the Government to provide funding support for existing lifts.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given the current profile of the current lift and escalator technicians, half of the resident workforce is likely to retire in the next 10 years.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the number of lifts and escalators increasing steadily, besides building up a pool of well-trained and skilled workers, we must rely on technology to improve our lift maintenance work processes and increase productivity.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With different usage pattern and number of lift landings in a single lift shaft, it may be more efficient to use intensity of usage, that is, mileage travelled as a gauge instead.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is similar to how cars should be sent for servicing after certain distance travelled.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Such mileage can be easily tracked using existing technology.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In addition, the use of technology can go a long way in enhancing the safety and welfare of our lift and escalator technicians.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Productive and innovative technology can reduce the maintenance work needed.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This will mandate lift and escalator companies to pay the local technicians the salaries that was agreed with the tripartite committee.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is an important step to attract workers, especially the younger ones, to this essential industry.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In English): In conclusion, while there is much to be done, I am heartened that the Government recognises the importance of the work of our lift and escalator technicians.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Besides ensuring that they have acquired competency so that the overall maintenance standards are raised, this new rule will help to enhance safety for the workers as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry share statistics on incidents resulting in injury?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope the Ministry could consider providing incentives to encourage L&E maintenance companies to tap upon technology to boost work safety for their staff at the elevator and escalator sites.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the area of lift breakdowns, what are the numbers in the following categories: public housing, non-public housing, commercial, industrial and institutional?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we further improve the reliability of L&E?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This could help to reduce downtime and minimise inconvenience.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   In the area of lift breakdowns, what are the numbers in the following categories: public housing, non-public housing, commercial, industrial and institutional?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we further improve the reliability of lifts and escalators (L&E)?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This could help to reduce the downtime and minimise inconvenience.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a densely built-up city state with more and more buildings rising above 20 storeys, it is very important that all the lifts installed are of good quality and are well maintained to ensure safety and reliability for all passengers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With a rapidly ageing society, lifts serve an increasingly essential role too, even in shorter buildings and facilities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In recent years, we have had a number of malfunctioning lift incidents, which had caused inconvenience and injuries.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is timely that we overhaul the relevant legislation and review the entire eco-system.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB is the largest builder and enjoys the benefit of economies of scale.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Presently, different projects are handled by different contractors, so I am concerned that this advantage may not have been fully exploited.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Should there be a need to have a central national storage for all the parts from the different lift manufacturers that have tendered successfully to install lifts for our flats and which have also undertaken to provide the parts for long-term maintenance?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The use of technology can assist to provide checks on the maintenance of lifts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the Ministry encourage the use of technology to monitor the performance of lifts round-the-clock independently, particularly to ensure lift safety?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has the current approach been adequate in preventing lift breakdowns?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many older lifts were installed without these features, which are specified in the latest standards.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such lifts could either be upgraded or replaced.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Last but not least, the most crucial element here is manpower, and I strongly support the various proposals to boost our pool of lift specialists and deepen their expertise.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is important that we have a strong Singaporean core of locally trained lift specialists, with attractive incentives for them to remain in this sector and to make career progress.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Workers will be able to look forward to a clear progression pathway which correlates the new certification requirements with wage increments for each role.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to increase the pool of Qualified Persons (QP) to meet inspection and maintenance enforcement requirements.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also fully support the proposal to introduce a new branch of specialist professional engineers in lift and escalator engineering.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I would like to conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Louis Ng asked why residential buildings and factories were not included under clause 17, which requires for existing buildings without basic accessibility features to provide these when undergoing addition and alteration works.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I mentioned earlier, all buildings built since 1990 have to comply with the Code on Accessibility, including the provision of basic accessibility features.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, buildings in the last 30 years are now compliant.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is a calibrated approach as we are mindful of the physical challenges in existing buildings as well as the cost impact to building owners.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The fund is available, and I urge them to do so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about maintenance of facades.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As mentioned earlier, we will put in place a new Periodic Facade Inspection (PFI) regime.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The regime provides a more structured approach towards the inspection and maintenance of facades so that owners can better meet their existing duty and enhance public safety.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap also asked about the regulation and training of personnel involved in facade inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Owners will need to appoint a competent person (CP) to carry out facade inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The CP must be either a professional engineer (PE) or registered architect, and can be assisted by facade inspectors (FIs) in carrying out inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, they do not have to do it all on their own, but there are roles such as FIs that they can use.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The FI must be a resident engineer, a resident technical officer, or any other person who possesses the relevant qualifications and experience.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: CPs and FIs must undergo a compulsory facade inspection course.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Since 2017, more than 200 individuals have successfully completed the course.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will also introduce inspection guidelines in due course to guide CPs and FIs in performing their duties.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These efforts will ensure that we will have a pool of qualified and competent personnel to support the new inspection regime.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For these courses, they can also tap on SkillsFuture subsidies available.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For those below 40 years old, they can get up to 50% subsidies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For older workers above 40, Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, they can get up to 90% subsidies too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To some extent, I think, if you look at the entire picture, we are trying to beef up our core capabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about the terms used in defining the persons responsible for maintaining building facades and about the responsibility for facade maintenance in HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The definition being amended relates to exterior features.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The maintenance of exterior features is part of any common property in HDB blocks that is currently covered under the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act, or BMSMA in short.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, the person responsible for such maintenance is defined in the BMSMA as the Town Council (TC) and not HDB.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition, the BMSMA's definition of "person responsible" includes the Town Council's contractor and the condominium's managing agents (MAs) as long as they have charge and control over common property.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What we have done – it looks a bit complicated – but we are basically porting over the clauses in the existing BMSMA into the current Building Control Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the BMSMA, it was the Town Council mentioned – no HDB.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But in the current Act, you do have HDB and Town Council.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is for retrofitting orders by the Minister.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That will still be retained under clause 13, in which the Minister can still designate retrofitting works to HDB and Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Just to clarify again, maintenance of exterior features and facades is under the Town Council and its contractors, for coverage of retrofitting, it is HDB and Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is no change effectively on the total outcome.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If found to be a design fault or construction issue, it will be 100% covered by HDB.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the scheme is in place and not so much part of the Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we have not changed the position when transferring the BMSMA provisions on maintenance of exterior features over to the Building Control Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked why clause 20 of the Bill amends the Act to no longer mandate that inspections ordered under section 24(1) be performed by an architect or professional engineer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: She asked if this would have an impact on public safety.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We expect most of the inspections to still be done by architects and professional engineers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, depending on the specific situation, specialists with the necessary skills and competencies, such as in building materials and components, may be better equipped to carry out such inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it depends on the type of issue involved.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The amendment allows for such specialists who may not be architects and PEs to be appointed to do inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, there should be no impact on public safety.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In fact, it should be better because now, you are allowing others with specialised engineering skills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Lim and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap noted that the PFI regime entails cost.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The schedule for the PFI has been set at seven years, to be tied in with the repairs and redecoration (R&R) schedule that TCs, MAs and Management Corporation Strata Titles (MCSTs) conduct, to save costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, you can also leverage on the gondolas that you set up, other things that you typically do in terms of painting of the building, for example, and you can leverage on some of these things to reduce cost.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will also work with owners responsible for many buildings to spread out the inspections in the initial phase to minimise any spikes in costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA is working on other measures to help manage costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These include building up the pool of CPs and FIs, and exploring, as some Members have also suggested, how technology can help to carry out inspections in a more effective and productive manner.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In terms of whether there will be co-sharing of costs or additional funding provided to Town Councils for the new facade inspections, as building facades are part of common property and under the purview of TCs, TCs are responsible for conducting regular inspections to ensure that the facades are in good condition.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I mentioned, the schedule of the PFI has been set at seven years, which can be tied in with the R&R schedule to save costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will also work with owners, including TCs to spread out inspections in the initial phase to minimise any spikes in costs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, BCA launched a grant call with HDB for the development of a drone inspection system to carry out automated facade inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This reduces manpower cost in terms of getting gondolas up and all the other necessary infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will continue to monitor this carefully as we take the safety of all our users very seriously.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, the number of lifts in Singapore is expected to grow.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We recognise Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap's concern that there should be enough skilled manpower to keep our lifts safe and in working condition.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is why we have been working with the industry to build up capabilities and capacities at all levels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Professional Engineers Board (PEB) introduced the specialist professional engineer (SPE) in lift and escalator engineering in 2017.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Their scope of work will increase with the new requirements under the Bill to also include the certification of new installations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To ensure that there continues to be enough competent personnel to inspect our lifts, BCA is working together with the Association of Consulting Engineers Singapore (ACES) and The Institution of Engineers, Singapore (IES) to train lift and escalator inspectors (LEIs).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Graduates and diploma holders in the mechanical or electrical engineering disciplines who have relevant experience will be able to apply for registration as LEIs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They will need to complete an LEI training course and pass an examination.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These efforts will grow the pool of L&E professionals to meet increasing demand.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As for lift maintenance technicians, BCA and ITE have introduced courses for the various competency levels in the PWM to provide them with common engineering knowledge and skills on servicing lifts and their key components.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Technicians will therefore be required to obtain the specialist level competency – so they must obtain this – before they are allowed to service lifts independently, once this regulation comes into effect.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I urge employers to start training up all the technicians.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are now giving a grace period before we put in the regulations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But this is the time as we have put in more support now with SkillsFuture and we need to help train and beef up our capabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The PWM provides a common competency and wage framework for all lift firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will benefit more than 1,000 local lift technicians and ensure that their remuneration is commensurate with their job responsibilities and competencies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA and ITE are also working with the industry to develop more courses to help lift technicians advance along their PWM career progression pathways.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will ensure consistency in training standards and facilitate job mobility, both of which were highlighted by Mr Zainal Sapari and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As mentioned by Mr Zainal, we have, indeed, been engaging our stakeholders actively to encourage the early adoption of PWM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the supply side, 40 lift firms, representing 95% of the market, have already committed to adopt the PWM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the demand side, all Government procuring entities now award tenders only to lift firms that have adopted the PWM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA has been in discussions with Town Councils, trade associations and chambers (TACs) and other major service buyers, who have also been supporting the PWM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We encourage service buyers to come on board early, to smoothen the transition to a mandatory one by 2022.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about extending the PWM to foreigners in the lift industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The intent of the PWM is to build a strong local core for the lift industry and not to discriminate against foreigners.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, Mr Ng will be happy to know that several lift firms that have committed to implementing the PWM have also indicated that they provide their foreign lift technicians with comparable remuneration packages.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, as they improve their skill-sets, competencies and productivity, their wages will also go up.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it has to be commensurate with the skillsets and skill pathways.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Beyond the PWM, we also agree with Mr Zainal and Mr Ng on the need to improve the working conditions in the lift sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA is working with the industry for new lifts to be designed with better working conditions for lift technicians as part of the work of the Tripartite Cluster for the Lift and Escalator Industry, which Mr Zainal chairs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, Mr Zainal, it is in your hands.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, I understand that the Committee is looking at measures relating to improving minimum illumination levels and mechanical ventilation in the lift shaft so that lift technicians can work in a cooler, brightly lit environment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And for existing lifts, we encourage lift owners to proactively incorporate these improvements as part of their planned upgrading or modernisation works.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Yes, the Tripartite Cluster can do its part and, certainly, we look forward to Mr Zainal's recommendations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, as we raise wages and improve the working environment, we will also improve the safety and productivity of the L&E industry through the use of technology, as suggested by many Members who have spoken today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One way is to use remote monitoring and diagnostics (RM&D), which enable lift contractors to not only monitor lift operations in real time remotely, but also to troubleshoot and diagnose faults with greater accuracy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Such systems are being used in some other countries in Europe and BCA is exploring with the industry how this can be applied in our local context.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, BCA is working to develop a common standard for these systems that will facilitate more pervasive deployment of such technologies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If successfully deployed in Singapore, RM&D technology could enable us to shift to a use-based or predictive maintenance regime, as suggested by Mr Zainal and Er Dr Lee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, it is very rigid in terms of monthly inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But that is because we do not have ways in which we can measure how often the lift is used and how far it travels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think, with technology, we are able to do it better and, therefore, we can assess how soon or how often your lifts need to be maintained much more accurately.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: RM&D can also change the way lift technicians work in the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: A technician will be able to monitor all the lifts under his charge from a remote location and in real time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, when a fault occurs, the system will provide the technician with the necessary information to diagnose the fault and to attend to it immediately.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will reduce the amount of time that the lift technician is required to spend doing maintenance work on site, which not only makes his job safer but also enables him to maintain a larger number of lifts, thus raising his productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think all these fit into the whole PWM narrative in which you want to see greater productivity, you want to see greater skill-sets and improved working conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, I think you can see the rationale of why we are localising this set of jobs and taking it to the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We want more Singaporeans to come on board.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about how we can ensure the adequacy of lift parts in order to meet the maintenance requirements under the Act, for example, by setting up a national storage for such parts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Instead, owners can take a preventive approach towards maintenance by planning ahead and scheduling replacement of lift components early, before they cause any issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The RM&D systems I spoke about earlier have the potential to help owners to do better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think it would not be practical to legislate that lift systems must be open and non-proprietary because doing so would severely limit the selection of lifts available to Singapore, given the lift designs of many of our international lift are actually quite proprietary.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Just like cars, it is very hard to interchange your parts between a Honda, Kia and Volkswagen, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, you have to also be mindful that there are very few of such models around.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On Mr Gan's question on HDB's procurement of lifts, while it is not relevant to the Bill, we should ask MOF on how you procure lifts in bulk.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I would like to assure the Member that HDB does enjoy the economies of scale in its lift procurement.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The drones can only be used during the weekend.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And certainly, as we expand the regulations to more Town Councils and across the board, I think this is where we can certainly do better.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I think I asked about higher insurance coverage for the workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is actually an MOM question but never mind.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, whether they have insurance or not, it is claimable.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: I was wondering whether MND has plans to subsidise the cost of retrofitting these lifts to make sure that we can actually create an environment conducive for the L&E technicians to work in.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I understand that is being worked on by your Cluster Committee.
